owner_scope: Institution-wide undergraduate first-year and transfer admissions, shared undergraduate financial aid/cost/housing, and central nonprofessional graduate application policy. Professional-school rules are out of scope.

applicant_categories: first-year; includes international applicants applying from secondary school

intakes: program-defined; central online application currently open for 2027 entry

facts.value: Applicants apply to Stanford University as a whole and are not admitted to a major, department, or school. A stated prospective major or career interest is nonbinding; choosing an undergraduate major is a post-admission study choice.
A person may submit at most three Stanford undergraduate admission applications total, counting first-year and transfer applications together. A person below the limit may reapply.
conditions: Counts prior undergraduate applications to Stanford across the two procedures.

facts.value: Apply online through the Common Application, including Stanford Questions. Applications open in early August; Stanford Questions are completed in the Common Application after adding Stanford.

scope.cycle: 2027-entry cycle as shown on current 2026 admissions pages

facts.value: Application fee is USD 100, nonrefundable. Request the Common App fee waiver and have a counselor/school official verify it in Common App or submit the completed NACAC form as directed. The application may be submitted before waiver approval; Stanford may request more information.

scope.cycle: 2027-entry cycle as shown on current 2026 admissions pages

conditions: This application fee is distinct from CSS Profile charges; Stanford does not issue CSS Profile fee-waiver codes.
exceptions: International students unable to pay CSS Profile fees or in a country where College Board cannot process payment may use Stanford's International Student Application for Financial Assistance for the aid process; this does not waive the admission fee.

facts.value: A high-school diploma or equivalent is required to enroll. Stanford publishes no prescribed set of required high-school courses. It recommends rigorous year-on-year study and mastery across English, mathematics, social studies, science, and world language, approximately five academic courses per semester including senior year; these are preparation recommendations, not stated course prerequisites.
conditions: The diploma/equivalent is an enrollment qualification; it need not be held when applying.

facts.value: ACT or SAT is required for first-year applicants. Stanford has no minimum score and no score guarantees admission. Either exam is accepted without preference; the redesigned ACT and original ACT are accepted, and the redesigned ACT science section is optional. Applicants self-report highest scores; official scores are required for self-reported scores if admitted and enrolling. SAT is superscored across highest Evidence-Based Reading and Writing and Math sections; ACT superscore may be reported with highest section scores. Writing/essay portions are optional. Stanford recommends tests within five years.

scope.cycle: 2027-entry cycle; ACT transition policy published from 2025-26 onward

conditions: Latest possible sittings published for the current cycle: REA ACT by end of September and SAT by end of October; RD ACT and SAT by end of December. Late scores may not arrive in time, and review is not delayed for them.
exceptions: AP exams are not mandatory, but all AP scores must be self-reported if taken. IB Diploma students outside the US must have predicted marks sent by a school official. British-system applicants must have GCSE results and predicted A-Level marks sent; Stanford says applicants generally have at least three full A-Level courses. These are distinct examination-document rules, not substitutes for ACT/SAT.

facts.value: The current Stanford page accepts both original and redesigned ACT versions and states the redesigned ACT science section is optional. It does not name a single SAT form/edition cutoff; SAT section superscoring is described. No exemption from the ACT-or-SAT requirement is published on the reviewed current first-year testing page.
exceptions: International applicants do not have an English-proficiency exam requirement for undergraduate admission; this is separate from required ACT/SAT.

facts.value: Required components include Common Application; school report and counselor recommendation; official high-school transcript/academic results (grades 9–12); and two academic-teacher recommendations. School officials/testing agencies must send official records directly; applicant-submitted transcripts are not accepted. Report international curriculum results and predictions when available. Any high-school, college/university, or online courses absent from the current high-school transcript require official records.
conditions: A midyear transcript is due February 15 for Regular Decision applicants, REA applicants deferred to RD, and REA admits. Students already graduated do not submit a midyear transcript. Final transcript with graduation date is due July 1 for admitted students who enroll.
exceptions: An optional additional recommender may submit a letter if they know the applicant well and offer new insight; this is in addition to the two required teacher letters.

facts.value: Besides the Common App personal essay, applicants answer several Stanford short questions (each up to 50 words) and write three Stanford short essays, each 100–250 words: an idea/experience that excites learning; a note to a future roommate; and a distinctive contribution based on life experiences, interests, and character.

For 2027 entry, REA Common Application deadline is November 1, with decisions by mid-December; RD deadline is January 5, with decisions by early April. Submit by 11:59 p.m. in the applicant's local timezone. REA is nonbinding. If admitted, reply by May 1. Application with Optional Arts Portfolio uses earlier application deadlines: October 15 REA and December 5 RD.
conditions: Stanford may evaluate and decide an application even if every component has not arrived. Current page lists mid-November/mid-February missing-document notifications.
exceptions: REA denial is final and the applicant may not reapply RD in that cycle. REA applicants face restrictions on applying to other institutions' early plans, with specified exceptions; applicants must check the official REA policy for their exact concurrent application pattern.

facts.value: First-year applicants who attend high school in an interview area and apply REA or RD may be invited to an optional alumni interview. Availability depends on interview-area coverage and volunteer availability; applicants cannot request or schedule one. Not receiving an interview is not a disadvantage.
conditions: Invitation and available alumni interviewer are required.
exceptions: No transfer interview policy has been established by this source; do not transfer this fact to the transfer procedure.

facts.value: Optional arts portfolios are available in Art Practice, Dance, Music, and Theater and Performance Studies for applicants wishing to show exceptional fine/performing-arts achievement. Portfolio submission does not require an arts major. Submission is through Stanford's portal after the Common Application; areas have specific materials. Music and Theater/Performance Studies may include an optional arts recommendation; none accepted for Art Practice or Dance. Mail-in items are not returned.
conditions: Portfolio deadline is October 20 for REA and December 10 for RD; Common App must be submitted October 15 / December 5 respectively. Transcript, School Report, and teacher evaluations may arrive by standard November 1 / January 5 deadlines. No extension is offered for an arts recommender.
exceptions: QuestBridge National College Match applicants cannot submit an Arts Portfolio because its timeline does not align with portfolio review.

facts.value: Undergraduate international applicants are reviewed in the context of the educational system, country, and school resources where they attend secondary school. The application process otherwise follows the same first-year or transfer route regardless of citizenship/residence. Undergraduate English-proficiency exams are not required; fluency in English is an admission prerequisite, and applicants may self-report English exam scores if they wish.
conditions: Citizenship/legal status matters separately for financial aid and is not inferred from where secondary school was attended.
exceptions: US citizens, permanent residents, and undocumented/DACA students are treated as domestic for undergraduate admission/aid status as the official FAQ specifies; aid-specific rules still depend on the applicable category.

facts.value: Stanford says it meets demonstrated need for admitted undergraduates regardless of citizenship when aid was requested during the application process. For international citizens, requesting aid is a factor in admission evaluation and makes the process more selective; an international citizen who applies without aid and enrolls after admission is generally ineligible to request undergraduate aid later. US citizens/permanent residents studying abroad remain domestic for aid evaluation.
conditions: The need-request choice must be made in the admission application; request and eligibility are distinct.
exceptions: The page describes an exception if an enrolled international student's citizenship status changes and they become eligible for federal student aid; aid may then be considered starting the quarter they become eligible. Confirm case specifics with Stanford Financial Aid.

facts.value: Anyone who earned college credit in an associate or bachelor's degree program after high-school completion must use the transfer route. High-school/college dual-enrollment students apply as first-year. Transfer credit must be from an accredited degree-granting institution; vocational, technical, performance, or professional-program credit is excluded. Applicants need a high-school diploma/equivalent/GED to enroll. Applicants with an earned bachelor's degree are not eligible for undergraduate admission.
conditions: The trigger is post-secondary degree-credit study after secondary school; high-school dual enrollment is expressly treated differently.
exceptions: No minimum number of completed credits or years is required. Stanford describes approximately two years of full-time, in-person college coursework by entry and consecutive full-time study as typical competitive preparation, not a formal minimum.

facts.value: Stanford permits at most 90 quarter units of transfer credit (approximately two full-time years). Transfer entrants must complete at least two years of full-time enrollment at Stanford to earn a bachelor's degree, regardless of prior coursework.

Official Stanford transfer pages conflict: the general Transfer Applicants requirements page lists USD 90; the dedicated Application Fee/Fee Waiver page says USD 100. Both describe a nonrefundable fee and Common App fee-waiver request. Do not display a single confirmed amount until Stanford resolves the discrepancy.
conditions: The dedicated fee page says submit Common App fee-waiver selection plus NACAC Transfer Fee Waiver form, and either attach Student Aid Report or obtain school official signature. Applicant need not wait for waiver approval before submitting; Stanford may ask for additional information.

facts.value: ACT or SAT is required for transfer applicants. There is no admission minimum or guaranteed-admission score. Self-report highest scores; official score reports are required from enrolled admits. Stanford accepts original and redesigned ACT forms; SAT is superscored across highest Math and Evidence-Based Reading/Writing sections; ACT superscore may be submitted. Stanford recommends results within five years.

scope.cycle: 2027-entry cycle; ACT transition policy published from 2025-26 onward

conditions: Latest possible sitting published: ACT by end of January and SAT by end of December for the annual transfer cycle; late scores may not arrive in time and review is not delayed.
exceptions: The reviewed official transfer testing page states ACT/SAT is required but does not state criteria for exceptions or waivers. Do not assert either that waivers exist or that none exist; ask Undergraduate Admission about an individual case.

facts.value: Required materials: Common Application; fee or fee-waiver request; official high-school transcript including graduation date (or equivalent); official transcript from every college/university attended; College Report completed by an official at current/most recent institution; and two academic-instructor recommendations. International leaving exams (A-levels, IB, national exams) must be sent directly by school/testing agency; any AP results taken must all be self-reported. Official school materials are arranged through the school official. A midyear college transcript is not required.
conditions: Stanford generally allows a grace period after the deadline for school-official materials not controlled by the applicant, and says late third-party items are not penalized; application review can proceed with missing items at Stanford's discretion.

facts.value: Transfer applicants submit a personal statement about reasons for transferring and objectives (250–650 words), several short responses (50-word limit), and Stanford short essays including a learning-excitement response (100–250 words), one choice between a roommate note or community definition/contribution essay (100–250 words), and a distinctive contribution response. Prospective major/career interests are nonbinding.

Transfer Common Application deadline is March 15 at 11:59 p.m. applicant local time. Missing-document notice is in April, decisions are released by mid-May, and admitted applicants reply by June 2. All new transfer entrants begin in autumn/fall; no winter or spring start is offered. The official page does not label a calendar year for this recurring deadline.
conditions: Stanford may decide an application even when some materials have not arrived.

facts.value: Transfer applicants may submit a reviewed optional portfolio in Art Practice, Dance, Music, or Theater and Performance Studies; portfolio submission does not require majoring in the arts. Application is due March 15 and materials March 20 through the Stanford portal. Music and Theater/Performance Studies may include optional arts recommendation letters; Art Practice and Dance do not accept these letters. Mailed items are not returned.

Published standard undergraduate budget for 2026–27 academic year (Autumn, Winter, Spring; typical full-time student): tuition USD 67,731; housing and food 22,944; student-fees allowance 2,610; books/supplies allowance 855; personal expenses allowance 3,405; travel varies; total USD 97,545. New first-year and transfer students also have one-time orientation USD 525 and document USD 250 fees included in their budget. Tuition, fees, housing, and food are billed quarterly; books, supplies, personal and travel amounts are planning allowances, generally not billed. Health insurance is required; Cardinal Care is assumed in budget for international students, while many other undergraduates waive it with other adequate coverage.

fee_status: standard undergraduate budget; not differentiated by fee status

conditions: The standard profile assumes unmarried, financially dependent student enrolled full-time for Autumn/Winter/Spring, living in residence hall or off-campus. Actual budgets differ; travel varies. Allowances are not fixed billed charges.
exceptions: International budget assumes Cardinal Care. For other students, Financial Aid may help with insurance costs if no adequate coverage and substantial need; zero expected parent contribution qualifies for scholarship coverage if no adequate coverage.

facts.value: Stanford describes undergraduate aid as need-based and says it meets demonstrated need for admitted applicants, including international citizens, who request aid during admission. It does not offer merit scholarships except a limited number of athletic scholarships. Domestic admission is need-blind; need can be considered for some international applicants. Estimate with the official net price calculator; aid is not a guaranteed reduction until assessed and awarded.
conditions: Aid is based on demonstrated family need; international applicants must indicate an aid request when applying for admission.
exceptions: The non-need-based athletic scholarship exception is limited; the site does not publish its full eligibility or award amounts in the reviewed shared policy pages.

facts.value: Priority filing dates and expected notification on Stanford's central new-student/continuing-student aid page: first-year REA November 15, aid notification mid-December; first-year RD February 15, notification early April; transfer March 15, notification mid-May; continuing student April 30, notification in August. These are aid application deadlines, separate from admission deadlines. The page does not state a specific entering academic year for the new-student priority-date table.
conditions: Required aid documents/forms differ by citizenship, REA/RD/transfer, and new/continuing student. Current detailed REA international aid checklist labels itself 2026–27; do not assume its documentation and tax-year rules automatically apply to 2027–28 entrants. Aid-seeking international students must indicate aid in the admission application. If CSS Profile payment is impossible or unavailable in country, the current checklist permits ISAFA. Divorced/separated/never-married parents submit separate CSS records; a noncustodial-parent waiver requires evidence.
exceptions: Continuing US citizen/eligible noncitizen institutional scholarship review requires CSS Profile, IDOC/tax documents, and FAFSA; CSS is not needed when seeking only federal/state aid. Continuing international applicants have their own CSS and student tax documentation. This fact is not a complete category-specific aid checklist.

facts.value: Financial aid is reassessed for continuing undergraduates each academic year rather than being a fixed four-year amount. For 2026–27, continuing US citizen/eligible noncitizen aid priority date is April 30 with CSS Profile/IDOC and FAFSA; institutional scholarship consideration requires CSS, FAFSA, and tax documents. Continuing international applicants file CSS Profile and required student tax documents by April 30; published award notification date is June 15. Students requesting scholarship beyond four years/twelve quarters must submit a Request for Extended Aid Eligibility.
conditions: Need-based award amount depends on renewed assessment and applicable financial documentation.

facts.value: For transfer entrants in the published 2026–27 aid checklist, US citizens/eligible noncitizens submit CSS Profile, FAFSA and IDOC (parent tax records); priority date March 15 and mid-May aid notification. CSS Profile, FAFSA and tax documents are all required for institutional scholarship; CSS is not required if seeking only federal/state aid. International transfer applicants use CSS Profile and International Student Supplement; Canadian citizens submit specified Canadian tax records through IDOC and do not submit the supplement. Applicants unable to pay CSS fee or in a country where payment is unavailable may use ISAFA. Divorced/separated/never-married parents submit separate CSS profiles; noncustodial-parent waiver requires supporting documents. International applicants must request aid in the admission application.

scope.cycle: 2026-2027 aid cycle as explicitly labelled by Stanford

conditions: These are the official 2026–27 checklists; do not carry tax years, forms, or publication timing forward to a later aid cycle without checking its edition.
exceptions: Undocumented applicants follow US timelines but do not file FAFSA; current transfer page should be checked for the relevant aid year and alternate undocumented-student documents.

facts.value: Published undergraduate aid types include need-based Stanford University Scholarship (CSS Profile-based; no separate application for individual scholarship funds), federal Pell and Supplemental Educational Opportunity grants (FAFSA-based, automatic consideration), student employment including Federal Work-Study/community-service work study, outside scholarships, and federal Direct/PLUS loans. Stanford says loans are not expected to meet ordinary college costs but may be requested. Stanford does not currently participate in California Student Aid Programs; institutional funds replace Cal Grant for most otherwise-eligible students, with rare stated exceptions. Need-based international aid is from institutional funds; international request affects admission review and aid is limited. A small number of athletic scholarships are the stated merit-aid exception.
conditions: Federal grants/loans require applicable federal eligibility; aid form and eligibility depend on citizenship category. Stanford aid offer, not generic availability, determines a specific student's award.
exceptions: Cal Grant may still apply in very rare cases for students otherwise ineligible for Stanford institutional aid; Stanford directs such students to provide the award notice.

facts.value: Matriculated frosh are guaranteed 12 complete or partial academic-year housing quarters; transfer students receive nine. Housing eligibility requires enrollment and application by the first housing deadline and participation in later rounds when needed. If a guarantee-space assignment is unavailable, guaranteed students are housed by the end of the first week, potentially in temporary guest rooms or graduate residences. Enrolled first-year students are required to live in a university-designated residence unless an exception is announced.
conditions: A housing guarantee does not guarantee a specific residence or quarter without meeting application deadlines. Housing is for enrolled matriculated degree-program students.
exceptions: For students more than seven years removed from high school, undergraduate-housing eligibility is restricted; qualifying students are directed to graduate housing. Couples/family options have their own category rules.

facts.value: Stanford undergraduate residences include live-in faculty or senior-staff Resident Fellows and trained residential staff; Residential Education programming is described as academic, social, and personal support. New frosh and transfer housing assignments are handled by R&DE Student Housing and are associated with the required first-year residence policy.

Stanford University is in Stanford, California, in the San Francisco Bay Area; Stanford's official postal location is Stanford, CA 94305, United States. Campus location and residential campus context do not determine applicant residency/fee classification.

Central minimum eligibility for graduate admission is a US bachelor's degree or recognized international equivalent held, or expected before enrollment, from a recognized institution, plus English proficiency. Each program may set higher or other admission requirements. International degree-specific equivalency guidance is maintained by Stanford; a WES report is not required at application but may be requested after an accepted offer for credential verification.
conditions: Program-specific degree level, field preparation, and prerequisites remain owned by each graduate program.
exceptions: Graduate Admissions university policy applies to graduate degree programs other than programs in the Graduate School of Business and Law and the MD/Physician Assistant Studies programs in Medicine; joint professional degrees require separate admissions. MLA and Honors Cooperative remain within this graduate policy, but have their own program-specific procedures. Coterminal/current-student pathways are separate.

facts.value: No TOEFL/IELTS application score is required when at least one central exemption applies: applicant is a US citizen or permanent resident; English is first language; applicant earned/will earn a US bachelor's, master's, or doctoral degree or international equivalent from a university where all instruction was in English; or has at least two consecutive full-time years of professional or educational experience conducted in English within the past 10 years. Experience must be entirely in English and total 24 consecutive months by application time. No additional evidence is required at application from self-reported qualifying cases; supporting documents may be requested after accepting an offer.
conditions: Applicants who do not qualify for any listed exemption must submit an official TOEFL iBT or IELTS Academic score at application.
exceptions: The central page advises applicants uncertain about English-experience eligibility to answer No and submit a test score. Program-specific higher English minima may still apply.

facts.value: Central minimum for admission consideration: TOEFL iBT 90 for tests taken before 2026-01-21; TOEFL iBT 4.5 for tests on/after 2026-01-21; IELTS Academic 7.0. These satisfy consideration only, not automatic admission. Program may impose a higher minimum. For tests administered on/after January 21, 2026, Stanford has adopted the redesigned TOEFL score scale; do not compare old and new numerical scales as if identical. TOEFL MyBest scores are accepted; official scores must be sent by ETS. IELTS scores are reported through the method on the central test page. English tests are valid two years; earliest published valid test dates for Autumn 2027-28 are Sept. 1, 2024. A score below 109 old TOEFL / 5.5 new TOEFL / 8 IELTS requires the Stanford English Placement Test before the first quarter; there are no exceptions to the placement-test rule.

applicant_categories: international and other applicants not meeting exemption

conditions: TOEFL and IELTS validity is two years; a graduate program may enforce a stricter validity window. The placement test cutoff is distinct from the admission-consideration minimum.
exceptions: Waived applicants may still receive an offer condition requiring supporting proof of the exemption. Programs may publish higher test minima. The 2027 KHS applicant guidance states that most graduate programs use TOEFL 5.5 (new scale), reflecting program-specific standards above the 4.5 central floor; KHS applicants must satisfy their selected program's requirement.

facts.value: GRE General and GRE Subject requirements are set by each nonprofessional graduate program as required, optional, or not considered. If required/optional, official reports go directly from ETS; Stanford's central 2027–28 validity table accepts scores dated September 1, 2021 or later, while programs can require a shorter validity period. A GRE fee-reduction waiver is available to US citizens/permanent residents who receive an ETS GRE Fee Reduction Voucher, even if the program does not require GRE.
conditions: Check the specific program's GRE status and accepted score validity.
exceptions: No shared GRE requirement can be inferred for all graduate programs.

facts.value: The central online application covers nonprofessional graduate programs. Applicant selects one program and entry term; normally only one program application per academic year is permitted, with the stated exception that two Biosciences PhD programs may be selected within one application. The selected program controls supplemental questions and any program-specific materials. Graduate Admissions operates the application and university-wide requirements; the academic program reviews applicants, sets additional criteria, issues decisions and communicates funding offers.
conditions: A separate application is required for professional programs; central Graduate Admissions rules here do not govern those routes.
exceptions: Biosciences PhD allows two program selections within a single application; do not treat this as a second general application allowance.

facts.value: Central application sections include personal background, program/entry-term selection, academic history, test scores, experience, recommendations, statements, program supplement, and additional information. List every post-secondary institution where enrolled in an undergraduate/graduate degree program and provide its unofficial transcript at application. Three academic or professional recommendations are required (up to four may be entered as backup); statement of purpose is required (recommended maximum 1,000 words), and optional Enriching the Learning Community statement is up to 500 words. Resume/CV guidance, program supplemental items, research/faculty interests, writing samples, and prompts vary by program. Non-English records must be accompanied by original-language records and complete literal professional/institutional English translations. Official transcripts/degree conferral documents are required for verification after offer acceptance and before enrollment.
conditions: Recommendation letters generally share the program application deadline unless the program states otherwise; late letters may be accepted into the file but are not guaranteed review. At least one recommender is strongly recommended to be a university professor familiar with academic work.
exceptions: This common checklist does not replace program-specific documents, portfolio/technical writing samples, or professional-school materials.

facts.value: Central fee for a nonprofessional graduate application is USD 125, nonrefundable, payable on submission by accepted card or US checking account. Waiver types include ETS GRE Fee Reduction Voucher for US citizens/permanent residents; good-standing participant in an eligible program; and a school-based waiver subject to the school's eligibility/capacity. Waiver must be requested before application submission, preferably at least 10 business days (two weeks) before program deadline. Late requests are not guaranteed review; after deadline requests are not permitted. Paying before approval ends waiver consideration and fees are not refunded.
conditions: Eligible-participation program list is for 2027 entry and is versioned; verify exact membership. School-based criteria and deadlines differ by school and sometimes degree level.
exceptions: Some graduate programs may have limited alternative waiver options; confirm on program site. KHS has no fee for its separate scholarship application but does not waive the Stanford degree-program application fee.

facts.value: Graduate application for 2027 entry is open. Each intended program sets its own deadline; no central universal submission date is published. Program may use interviews. The program communicates its admission decision and offer response deadline; applicants must respond by the program deadline. If admitted and accepting, official transcripts/degree documents are sent to central Graduate Admissions for verification; matriculation follows successful credential review. International students have an enrollment hold until arrival on campus.
conditions: Application, funding, response, enrollment, and supporting-document dates must be collected at the exact program level; shared portal does not imply shared deadlines or offer conditions.
exceptions: Professional-school applications are separate and excluded from this central process.

facts.value: The selected nonprofessional graduate program communicates any offer of financial support. Stanford's Graduate Admissions FAQ says applicants in most cases are considered for available departmental funding when they apply and do not need a separate application, but this does not establish a universal award or funding type. Funding availability, eligibility, amount, terms, renewal, and deadline are program- and degree-specific.
conditions: Do not interpret application as guaranteed consideration in every program or as a funded offer.
exceptions: This shared fact excludes professional-school funding and the separately applied Knight-Hennessy scholarship.

facts.value: Graduate funding types include departmental/school/external fellowships, scholarships or grants; research and teaching assistantships (salary plus tuition allowance for service); hourly university work; and student loans. Stanford states continuous 12-month funding for enrolled PhD and DMA doctoral students in good academic standing for up to the first five years, assembled from external or Stanford fellowships and research/teaching assistantships as tailored to program. Some master's students may receive fellowships/assistantships, but most must seek outside funding or loans. Need-based/federal loan aid is requested separately through FAFSA and Stanford's Graduate Student Loan Application; international students generally are not federally eligible and should first contact their department for support.

scope.cycle: published policy checked 2026-10-02; loan form edition 2026-2027

conditions: Five-year doctoral funding statement is expressly limited to enrolled PhD/DMA students in good academic standing and up to the first five years; combination and amounts depend on program. Departmental funding and loan need are distinct.
exceptions: The institutional 12-month guarantee named by the source covers PhD and DMA, not all doctoral/professional awards. Do not extend it to master's or professional programs.

facts.value: The Stanford Bulletin states that a graduate program must not offer unconditional acceptance until Graduate Admissions confirms verification of academic credentials and English proficiency. After accepting an offer, the student must provide official transcripts and degree documents for verification before matriculation; international students have an enrollment hold until they arrive on campus. The Bulletin reserves withdrawal of offers in cases including application misrepresentation or serious lack of judgment or integrity.
conditions: Offer response/enrollment dates and any program-specific conditions remain set by the selected program and actual offer letter.
exceptions: The central policy's English exemptions and evidence review do not establish the professional-school admissions conditions.

value.boundary: Tuition additional; insuranceannualcost capturedAW/S, notextra summerinsurance. Rent/food/personal/transport/books areplanningallowances; actualhousingassignmentdiffers. Offcampus estimate10-40percenthigher. Firstyearmoving/technology costsanddependentcarecan vary; documentedexpensesmayadjustloanbudget. STEPfourquarterbudgetisdistinct.

conditions: Tuition omitted from these totals; specific program/unit tuition must be added separately.

facts.value: Knight-Hennessy Scholars (KHS) is a separate competitive scholarship/program, not a degree or direct route into Stanford. For 2027 cohort, applicant must separately be admitted to and enroll in an eligible full-time Stanford graduate degree and hold first bachelor's degree earned January 2020 or later (January 2018 or later for military-service extension); current students may qualify if completing first degree by September 2027 under page criteria. Any nationality may apply. Exclusions include Honors Cooperative Program, Master of Liberal Arts, JSD/MLS, current PhD students adding same-discipline MA/MS, and coterminal degrees except current coterminal students applying externally to a new full-time degree beginning with KHS in same year. KHS offers cannot be deferred: a selected scholar unable to enroll must apply again for the intended year. First-year Stanford PhD candidates may combine eligible ARCS, dissertation-completion, Lieberman, RAISE, SGF or SIGF fellowships with KHS under the page criteria, but not CCSRE graduate fellowships or Shoucheng Zhang fellowship; those excluded awards cannot be discontinued to apply for KHS.

applicant_categories: all nationalities; separately eligible graduate applicants

conditions: Scholar status requires both KHS selection and admission/enrollment to an eligible Stanford graduate degree. Eligibility rules are cohort-specific and may change.
exceptions: KHS is not a JD/MD/MBA admission policy; excluded or professional programs must be checked in their own admissions route. KHS may not defer scholar offers.

facts.value: For the 2027 cohort, separate KHS application closes October 6, 2026 at 1 p.m. Pacific Time. Candidate must also submit a separate graduate program application by the earlier of the program deadline designated for KHS applicants or December 1, 2026. MBA applicants must meet MBA Round 1. The scholarship application has no fee; graduate-program application fee remains separately payable or waivable through that program's process.
conditions: For already admitted-and-deferred 2027 students or eligible 2026-starting PhD second-year students, the KHS page says a second degree-program application is not required.
exceptions: KHS timing does not modify admission deadlines for non-KHS applicants.

facts.value: KHS funding is tied to the degree listed in the initial award letter and provides tuition/associated-fee fellowship, living/academic stipend, and economy-class annual travel stipend for up to three years. Newly enrolling scholars receive a one-time relocation stipend; scholars in years two and three may apply for academic-enrichment funds. Public degree table: MA/MBA/MFA/MPP/MS/JSM/MLS/LLM up to six academic quarters (1–2 years); JD nine academic quarters; MD up to 11 quarters (excludes summer of first year); PhD/DMA up to 12 quarters including three summers; JD/MBA nine quarters; MSTP/MD-PhD up to 12 quarters including summers. Program-specific funding supplies additional years: MD years 4–5 under Medical School's standard commitment; PhD/DMA year 4 onward; MSTP year 4 onward under degree-program support. Funding for an additional graduate program may be requested up to KHS's three-year maximum but is not guaranteed. Stipends are taxable; KHS does not reimburse associated taxes.

conditions: KHS provides funding for the listed degree in the initial admission letter. Beyond-KHS funding is determined by each degree program's standard commitment; ask the school about individual details. Additional-degree KHS funding is discretionary, not guaranteed.

facts.value: The 2027 KHS application requires online background/application form, one-page US Letter resume in reverse chronological order, undergraduate and (if applicable) graduate transcripts, any tests required by the selected degree program, two recommendation letters, three short answers, and one essay. Short answers: academic/professional intent (250 words); engagement with a different perspective, courage, and falling short (250 combined); eight improbable facts (150 combined). Essay prompt asks how life influences shaped the applicant (550 words). Recommendations are due with KHS deadline and may be academic, community, or professional; letters must be written in English. Invitation-only later stages are video statement and finalist experience. KHS and degree-program applications are separately and concurrently evaluated; the program's required test scores are also due to KHS by the later of its deadline and the KHS deadline.
conditions: KHS has no minimum GPA/test score; applicant must meet any minima set by selected graduate program. KHS recommendations and graduate-program recommendations have distinct prompts/reviewers and may use different recommenders.
exceptions: KHS application cannot be edited after submission except test scores, recommenders, resume, and intended Stanford graduate programs. Invitation-only video/finalist stages apply only to selected applicants.

facts.value: Stanford evaluates international first-year applicants in the context of their school/country and does not require conversion of marks to a US GPA or prefer a national curriculum over A-Level/IB/AP. Applicants should complete the coursework that qualifies them for bachelor-level university study in their own education system and hold the secondary diploma/equivalent by enrollment. Official transcripts, teacher recommendations, marks and predictions must come directly from school officials/testing agencies; transcripts and teacher recommendations must be translated into English and original copies submitted when applicable. The reviewed central Stanford pages do not specify an equivalency ruling for a named Kazakh secondary diploma or country-specific score threshold.

WES is not required at initial application; its recommendation for uncertain equivalence during application is a separate advisory step.

facts.value: International newly admitted undergraduates and graduate students receive a Bechtel Connect invitation after accepting their Stanford offer to request initial immigration documents. Stanford issues F-1 I-20 or J-1 DS-2019; completed requests are typically processed within four weeks for undergraduates and four to six weeks for graduate students. Undergraduate proof of funding covers one year. Graduate I-20 proof covers nine months/three quarters; J-1 DS-2019 proof covers the full degree. Graduate international students retain an enrollment hold until arrival; F-1/J-1 students must enroll full time to maintain status. I-20/DS-2019 and visa applications are post-offer steps, not admission requirements.

facts.value: All new Stanford students, including frosh, undergraduate transfers, and graduate students, must complete entry health requirements: immunization records, screening, and when indicated testing/forms. Current public page lists August 15, 2026 for Autumn 2026 entrants and marks Autumn 2027 date not yet published; winter/spring 2027 dates are TBD. Requirements differ for standard nonmedical versus medical/PA students. Medical or religious exemption requests must be filed by the published deadline for the entry quarter. Vaden's 2026 guidance says nonmedical students require MMR documentation and TB screening, with other vaccines recommended or risk-specific; medical/PA requirements are more extensive.

facts.value: Stanford's published 2026–27 first-year aid checklists distinguish Restrictive Early Action from Regular Decision and domestic/eligible-noncitizen/undocumented from international applicants. For US citizens and eligible noncitizens, CSS Profile (school code 4704), FAFSA (001305), and IDOC parent 2024 federal tax returns/forms are due Nov 15 for REA (mid-December notice) or Feb 15 for RD (April notice). If parents are divorced, separated or never married, each completes a CSS Profile and both submit tax documents; FAFSA parent is the parent providing more support. A noncustodial-parent waiver requires signed request and supporting documentation through IDOC. CSS Profile, FAFSA and IDOC are needed for institutional scholarship; CSS is not required if seeking only federal/state aid. Undocumented students follow domestic dates and submit CSS Profile/tax documents but do not file FAFSA. International aid applicants must request aid on the admission application and submit CSS Profile plus the International Student Supplement; Canadian citizens submit 2024 Canadian tax statements through IDOC and do not submit the supplement. If an international applicant cannot pay the CSS fee or College Board payments are unavailable in their country, the current checklist permits ISAFA instead. For international REA, priority date is Nov 15/mid-December notification; RD is Feb 15/April notification. Divorced/separated/never-married parents each complete CSS; a noncustodial-parent waiver requires evidence through Document Upload.
conditions: These forms and tax-year instructions are expressly labeled 2026–27 and do not establish the exact 2027–28 applicant checklist. For international applicants, aid request at admission is a condition of later institutional-aid eligibility.
exceptions: Undocumented students do not file FAFSA. Only Canadian citizens use the specified Canadian tax-IDOC substitution and omit the International Student Supplement. ISAFA is an alternative only when CSS payment is unaffordable or unavailable, not a general replacement.

facts.value: REA applicants cannot also apply to a private US university under EA, REA, ED or Early Notification, or to a public university under binding early admission. Other RD applications are allowed; after Stanford denial or deferral, EDII elsewhere is allowed. Concurrent exceptions include nonbinding public early admission, nonbinding rolling admission, nonbinding non-US admission, military academies, and nonbinding early submission required for scholarship or special-program consideration. MIT EA is explicitly excluded. Deferred applicants send the provided update form rather than reapply.
conditions: These restrictions apply to REA, not Stanford Regular Decision or transfer.

facts.value: KHS permits limited brainstorming, organizing the applicant's own ideas, identifying unclear passages, and light grammar/spelling edits preserving meaning and voice. It prohibits generated draft responses, substantive outlines or narrative frameworks, significant rewriting/paraphrasing, generated experience reflections or conclusions, and material not primarily the applicant's own writing. The applicant remains responsible for authenticity.
